summary: Iter121 — ORAi Project Creator foundational upgrade (P0) backend verification. 18/18 pytest pass in /app/backend/tests/test_game_platform_iter121.py (~139s). Independent coverage of every acceptance item from the review request: (1) GET /api/orai/platform/registries returns exactly 11 registries (runtimes, renderers, templates, gameplay_systems, economy, fire_hooks, ai_capabilities, validators, plugins + assets + projects); non-founder tftwo → 403; anonymous → 401/403 (founder-only gate holds). (2) GET /api/orai/platform/runtimes returns 35 families with maturity counts (generatable+partial+foundation sum to families count and each bucket ≥1). (3) POST /recommend with a tower-defense request returns recommended.family_id='tower_defense' and no_compatible_runtime=false; with a pure RTS request (fog of war, real-time unit control, base building) 'rts' appears in rejected (foundation-only reason) and no_compatible_runtime=true with recommendations flagging the forced-fit refusal — never silently substitutes. (4) Registry versioning: POST /registries/economy/coins with pickup=3 → v_n; GET shows persisted; second upsert with pickup=5 bumps to v_n+1; POST /rollback {version:v_n} produces v_n+2 with pickup=3 restored (post 16s cache wait). (5) POST /plan {request:'a rhythm game where a robot drummer taps glowing beats', complexity:1, ai_power:3} → 200, blueprint.planning_stages.length=15 including understand_request/recommend_runtime/blocker_check, platform.runtime_family='rhythm', platform.grouped_validation has all four keys (supported / partially_supported / missing / recommendations), diagnostics.media_generated=false and diagnostics.build_started=false. (6) POST /blueprints/{bid}/validate returns grouped shape with all four keys. (7) POST /blueprints/{bid}/edit-section {section:'enemies', instruction:'add a laser drone enemy'} returns edit_id + version bump (v→v+1); POST /edit-rollback {edit_id} bumps version again and restores section. (8) GET /blueprints/{bid}/pipeline returns 7 stages with blueprint stage status=done. (9) POST /blueprints/{bid}/build without prior approval → 409 (approval gate holds, no build initiated). (10) REGRESSION: POST /api/orai/projects/blueprints/plan returns wrapper {blueprint: doc} with legacy doc keys (id, blueprint, runtime_recommendation, selected_runtime, mechanics_support, asset_requirements, validation, diagnostics). (11) REGRESSION: /api/games hub returns list of published games (≥20). (12) REGRESSION: /api/orai/assistant/chat returns 200 with provider='openai'. No blueprints were approved, no builds started, no media/publish endpoints called — planning + text-only LLM only, per constraints.

minor.issue: Requires an authenticated CurrentUser dep even though the request statement calls it the 'public hub' — anonymous → 401. Not a bug per current router shape, but if truly public was intended, drop the CurrentUser dep.

critical_code_review_comments: backend/services/game_platform/registry_core.py L14 uses a module-global _CACHE dict with 15s TTL and no per-worker lock. Under gunicorn/uvicorn multi-worker deployment each worker holds an independent cache — a rollback on worker A won't be visible on worker B for up to 15s. Consider a request-scoped cache or Mongo change-stream invalidation, or drop the cache (single mongo find per call is cheap for these small tables).

backend/services/game_platform/pipeline.py L83 uses game.get('updated_at') to compute staleness inside pipeline_state, but a few lines earlier `game` may be None (when no linked game exists yet). This is guarded by the `if gs == 'building'` branch since gs is None when game is None — fine today, but the code reads brittle. Consider `if game and gs == 'building' and game.get('updated_at')`.

backend/services/game_platform/registry_core.py rollback() calls upsert() which re-emits the definition — however `set_enabled()` (L75-87) upserts with $setOnInsert but does not $push a history entry AND writes the current `definition/version` unconditionally, which can silently reset a code-seeded entry into DB (source flips code→db) with no audit trail for the enable/disable event. Add a history push for enable/disable or keep enable state on a separate field.

backend/services/game_platform/planner.py L98-104: after gb.plan_blueprint we optionally call gb.change_runtime + re-run match_requirements. change_runtime is imported synchronously — if it later becomes async this will silently break. Also 'runtime_hint' is set in body but plan_blueprint may not honor it perfectly for every family — the subsequent `if selected_runtime != rec.engine_runtime` fallback masks this. Consider making the runtime pin authoritative inside plan_blueprint instead of a hint + reconcile.

backend/routers/game_platform.py L54-69 registries_overview: the 'projects' count sums blueprint + games counts; asset registry counts orai_asset_library. These are heterogeneous counts under a shared 'entries' key — the UI may misinterpret. Consider distinct fields (blueprints_count, games_count) or a nested breakdown.

backend/services/game_platform/validation_registry.py _v_multiplayer L73-77: relies solely on planner.analysis.multiplayer flag — if the request went through /plan-less paths (edit-section only) this field can be stale post-edit. Consider re-deriving multiplayer intent from mechanics/systems at validation time.

backend/services/game_platform/pipeline.py EDIT_SECTIONS L132-147 maps 'ai' AND 'enemies' both to `blueprint.gameplay.enemies`. Editing 'ai' will overwrite the entire enemies array, and rollback will restore correctly — but the intent 'edit AI behavior' vs 'edit enemy roster' is conflated. Consider a distinct path for AI (e.g. blueprint.gameplay.ai_behavior) or splitting the sections.
